descriptionChirho: Qal verb meaning to exult, rejoice greatly, expressing deep joy and triumphant gladness, typically directed toward God or in response to divine deliverance. Found in Hannah's prayer (1 Sam 2:1 'my heart exults in YHWH'), Psalms of praise (Ps 5:11; 9:2; 25:2; 68:3), wisdom literature (Prov 11:10; 28:12), and the Song of Moses (1 Chr 16:32). Multilingual glosses confirm a uniform semantic field: Arabic 'ibtahaja/yabtahij' (exult), German 'exult', Korean 'jeulgeowohada' (rejoice), Spanish 'exultar/regocijar'. All Qal inflections (perfect, imperfect, cohortative, infinitive, with and without conjunctive waw) represent the same core verbal sense of joyful exultation.
